source_reading.title: To J. S. Henslow, 12 November 1833

figure_contexts.quote: I have one mutilated skeleton of the animal of which I sent the jaw with 4 small teeth.

source_reading.assessment: Darwin's figure is embedded directly after his reference to the jaw with four small teeth. It is a surviving illustration attached to an otherwise complete outgoing letter, while the visual itself does not identify a particular earlier Henslow prompt.

source_reading.title: To J. S. Henslow, March 1834

figure_contexts.quote: some part of the skeleton of an animal, of which I formerly sent the jaw, which had four teeth on each side in shape like this.

source_reading.assessment: Darwin embeds a second jaw-tooth sketch while discussing another imperfect Megatherium head and the previously sent jaw. The figure is preserved and visually distinct in its terminal stroke from the downloaded 229 image at the viewed resolution; that rendering difference is a source-fidelity observation, not proof of different anatomical subjects or a new correspondence edge.
